To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

trimethylamine (a substance that has recently been found in fish effluents and that induces a phototactic reaction) does not induce a similar life-history reaction as fish kai- romones in Daphnia and that the direction of some reactions to TMA was similar but different for others such like size at maturity, compared to fish kai-romones.
Daphnia respond to trimethylamine with similar life-history traits as they do to fish kaironomes but that the directions of the responses are not always the same.
Daphnia clones react differentially to TMA and that the directions of life-history responses are similar for both fish kairomome and TMA, although the magnitudes are not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of fish kairomoncs, trimethylamine and a mixture of both substances on life-history traits of Daphnia.
the question whether TMA can induce the same life-history reactions in cladocerans as the kairomones released from the fish.
the question whether trimethylamine is the primary causative agent in fish induced changes of Daphnia and whether D. hyaline and D. galeate are less sensitive to fish kai-romones than D. magna.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Daphnia are able to respond in a life-history relevant way to trimethylamine but the reaction is not similar to that induced by fish kairomonones.
Daphnia are capable of responding to fish kairomo nes and trimethylamine, but the responses are not identical.

TMA is a secondary factor in the fish induced life-history reactions in daphnids, which is supported by the fact that the reaction norms for both factors (fish kairomone versus TMA) were similar in the same clone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Daphnia can react to a variety of different chemical stimuli in a similar manner and that the reaction norms are species and clone dependent.
Daphnia can respond to TMA, but the reaction patterns differ from those to fish kairo-mones.

TMA is not the primary chemical agent inducing fish induced life-history reactions in daphnids, but that it is a substance, which is released by fish and may be involved in the induction process of these reactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reaction of Daphnia clones to fish kaironomes is not universal.
TMA is a substance, which can induce life-history adaptations in cladocerans, but that these adaptations do not resemble those caused by fish kairomonones.
the chemical composition of fish kairomomes may be complex, and it is possible to separate the chemical components of fish kairo-mones and study the effects of each chemical separately.
